acceptanceCriteria: A Codex review run launched with codex exec -s read-only from a linked worktree cannot create or mutate tickets in the primary checkout's native Tasks journal, or the limitation is documented with the supported confinement.
The repository's Codex review route (docs or skill) states how a review-only run is kept from writing tickets, and a reproduction shows no new ticket after a read-only review.
body: Observed 2026-10-11 across five Codex review runs (codex exec -m gpt-6.1-sol -s read-only, run from linked worktrees under /private/tmp/claude-501): the reviewer created native tickets V1-1245, V1-1247, V1-1248, V1-1249, V1-1250, V1-1251, V1-1252, V1-1253, V1-1254 and V1-1255 in the primary checkout's store (journal under the primary .git/taskman) even though the orchestrator and lanes never wrote them. The issue #814 lane's round-2 log shows  and  output for V1-1252 and V1-1255. Expected: a read-only review cannot mutate the shared native queue. Actual: the sandbox flag does not confine corvint-tasks writes (the journal lives outside the worktree, possibly reachable through a non-filesystem path or a writable-root default), so review findings appear as unrequested tickets that need deduplication. Installed Tasks build407. Workaround in use: review prompts now say not to run ticket or task-store commands. Suspected rather than confirmed: the exact write path that escapes the read-only sandbox has not been isolated.

completion.reason: ALREADY-DELIVERED: commit ba16a6b83 (on origin/main) adds the ATR-V0-212 read-only guard refusing task-store mutations from read-only review runs; documented in docs/TASKS-SUPERVISION.md. Verified by tasksperf-1021o lane (PR #1486). Live Codex reproduction filed as a residual ticket.

title: Codex read-only review runs still create tickets in the primary native Tasks store
